_note: Hand-maintained search aliases, keyed by upstream exercise id (§5.4).
The dataset ships instructions in ten languages and Portuguese is not one of
them, so Portuguese search finds exactly what is written here and nothing
Seeded from the owner's actual program (M3, 2026-08-16) — the 21 exercises of
the Legs & Glutes / Push / Pull split, resolved from the program as built in
the app. The compound-lift set that stood in before M3 is kept rather than
replaced: those aliases work, and a lift not in today's program is exactly
what someone reaches for when changing one.
Accents are written naturally; search strips them before matching, so
'flexao' finds 'flexão'. PT-BR synonyms are included where the term genuinely
differs from PT-PT (gémeos / panturrilha, cadeira flexora / mesa flexora).
The build fails on an id that is not in the catalogue, so a typo here cannot
silently produce an alias nothing will ever match.
One ranking trap, learned in M3. An alias that exactly equals a query scores
900 and an alias that merely starts with it scores 700, and ties break on the
shorter English name. A bare 'agachamento' on any record would therefore
outrank 'barbell full squat', which is what the catalogue test asserts. Add
qualified aliases ('agachamento livre'), not bare ones.
